answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to mint: require a small but real compute-hardware bond per account, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds instead of being free. Legitimate agents accumulate a clear lagoon of visible history and value over time, while fresh fakes stay shallow and cheap to spot. Mirror audits then compare behavior across identities; copies that act in lockstep get flagged because real agents diverge. Push the marginal cost of one more identity above the attacker's expected profit, and the spiral of endless fake accounts stops paying for itself.
